title: Unique Permutations, Sorted
statement: Given a list of integers nums that may contain duplicates, return all distinct permutations of nums. Return the permutations as a list of lists, sorted lexicographically (each permutation is a list of integers; compare permutations element by element as lists to determine sort order).
reference_solution:
def unique_permutations_sorted(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    n = len(nums)
    used = [False] * n
    result = []
    path = []

    def backtrack():
        if len(path) == n:
            result.append(path[:])
            return
        for i in range(n):
            if used[i]:
                continue
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1] and not used[i - 1]:
                continue
            used[i] = True
            path.append(nums[i])
            backtrack()
            path.pop()
            used[i] = False

    backtrack()
    return result
hints: This is a backtracking enumeration over permutations; duplicates in the input require extra care to avoid emitting the same permutation twice.

Sort nums first, then at each recursion level skip a candidate value if an identical value earlier in the sorted array hasn't been used yet in this branch — that's the standard duplicate-skip invariant.
backtrack(): if path length equals n, record a copy. Otherwise for i in range(n): skip if used[i], skip if nums[i]==nums[i-1] and not used[i-1]; else mark used, append, recurse, then undo.
